Subject: Request: regional data-flow confirmation + PrivateLink topology

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo last week — Bluehaven is close to finalizing our list of vendors for the inference layer. Our InfoSec & procurement teams need a short written confirmation of how Redwood will ensure regional data locality and a simple sketch of the PrivateLink / peering topology for our onboarding packet.

What we need for our auditors by next Tuesday (2027-04-13):
- A plain-language statement of the egress/egress points for customer workload data (where app layer tokens and model outputs transit) for both US and EU deployments.
- A network sketch showing PrivateLink endpoints, VPC peering (if any), and where the operator-managed keystore (KMS) lives.
- Any required steps for us to configure an allowlist (IP/CIDR or peer IDs) on our side.
- A checklist of artifacts you can provide (SOC 2 report, SOC2 scope note, SIG/CAIQ answers, runbook excerpt).

Attachments: none yet on our side.

Can you confirm you can provide the sketch and a short statement by EOD Monday (2027-04-12)? If that’s tight, let me know a firm deliverable date.

Thanks,
Elena Morales

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can get you a concise package covering the points you listed. I’m looping in Jonas (network/runtime), Kimberly (security/compliance) and Grace (onboarding/ops) to assemble a short statement + a one-page sketch.

Quick answers up front:
- Primary egress: traffic for a tenant configured in the US will egress from us-east-1 only; EU-tenants will egress from eu-west-1 only. There is no cross-border transit for tenant inference traffic when you select the regional deployment option in the control plane.
- Private connectivity: we support AWS PrivateLink and VPC Peering depending on customer preference; the sketch will show both patterns.
- Keystore: customer keys (if you bring-your-own) remain in your KMS; Redwood's operator keystore for platform credentials is in a separate, auditable KMS partition per region.

We can deliver by EOD Monday (2027-04-12). Attached is a first-pass sketch (edge-zone-sketch.png) and a short checklist of the artifacts we'll include. Jonas/Kimberly — can you confirm the CIDR/peer-id values we should publish for an allowlist? Grace — any onboarding notes to include?

Best,

Aisha —

Thanks for the ping. A few clarifications and a short technical note to include in the package to Bluehaven:

1) Egress boundaries: For tenants we offer two deployment modes — regional (recommended for residency) and shared-hosted. When configured as regional, inference request/response token streams are routed to model shards pinned to the matched region. That means egress originates from that region's VPC subnets and NAT egress IPs only.

2) Private connectivity patterns:
- PrivateLink (recommended): one or two PrivateLink endpoints per region (depending on HA) in the customer's account. No cross-region transit.
- VPC Peering: supported for dedicated-private deployments; peering is strictly regional in our standard topology.

3) Keystore and keys:
- BYOK: we reference customer KMS ARNs and never export private keys.
- Operator KMS: separate AWS accounts per region with an auditable key-rotation policy.

4) Allowlist details: please publish the following in the package as the canonical allowlist: a small set of ASGs and ephemeral NAT egress IP ranges. I’ll attach the CSV with the current circuit list.

Note: we need to confirm whether Bluehaven uses any third-party CDN that terminates TLS before reaching the PrivateLink. If they do, we should call out how TLS termination affects the egress guarantee.

Attaching: privatelink-circuit-list.csv (internal), will redact before we send external.

—Jonas
Head of Cloud Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Elena —

Attached is a short package that meets your auditors' checklist: a one-page sketch of the PrivateLink & regional topology, a two-page checklist of artifacts we can provide, and a sanitized circuit list for allowlisting. Key points summarized below for ease of review:

- Regional residency: When you select the regional deployment option, Bluehaven tenant inference traffic will originate and terminate inside the configured region (us-east-1 for US, eu-west-1 for EU). No cross-border model-serving transit is performed by default.
- Private connectivity: Option A (PrivateLink) is our preferred pattern and avoids peering across customer VPC boundaries; Option B (VPC Peering) is available for dedicated customers and remains regional only.
- KMS: BYOK supported; operator keys are in regionally partitioned KMS accounts and are auditable.
- Allowlist: we include the sanitized list of PrivateLink ENIs/cidr ranges in the attachment. If you require peer IDs instead of IP ranges, let us know and we’ll add both.

Attachments (external): edge-zone-sketch.png, privatelink-checklist.pdf
Related: HS-9341 (our HubSpot record), https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b-edge-zone-sketch

If you want, I can schedule a 30-min walkthrough next week with Jonas and Kimberly to go over the sketch and the SOC2/SIG artifacts we’ll include in the formal evidence packet.

Best regards,
Aisha Rahman
